Heredó siendo niño y se convirtió en el: He became a child and became the first Duke of Savoy in 1416. The range elevation did not create a new dynasty.
Heredó siendo niño, con una regencia en: He became a child, with a regency in which his half-brother Valerano highlighted. His long government kept Saluzzo between the Savoyard pressures and French protection.
Welf inheritance of the County of Diepholz.
Herencia de 1392, con ámbitos territoria: The 1092's inheritance with territorial domains dated and the great western extension is documented about 1410.
Herencia de Eisenbach por los Riedesel y: The Riedesel inheritance of Eisenbach led to a gradual jurisdictional dispute, without immediate legal independence.
Hermana de Carlos XII, fue reconocida re: Sister of Charles XII, he was recognized queen of Sweden in 1719 in exchange for accepting a constitution that limited real power. In 1720 he abdicated in favor of her husband, Federico de Hessen-Kassel.
Hermana de Guillermo I y Reinaldo IV de: Sister of William I and Reinaldo IV of Guelders, she was the mother of Mary of Arkel. His offspring explains Arnoldo's claim in 1423. The succession was not a direct father-son relationship between Reinaldo and Arnoldo.
Hermana de Guillermo de Holanda, se casó: Sister of William of Holland, she married John of Avesnes. Through her, their son John II was related to the comital house of Holland. That connection proved decisive in 1299, when the death of John I of Holland allowed the inheritances of Holland and Hainaut to be united.
Hermana de Magnus Eriksson e hija de Ing: The sister of Magnus Eriksson and daughter of Ingeborg of Norway. He married Albert II of Mecklenburg. His son Albert was king of Sweden, while his son Henry's offspring took to Erik of Pomerania. It is a key connection between Bjälbo, Mecklenburg and the Kalmar union.
Hermana del zar búlgaro Iván Alejandro y: Sister of the Bulgarian Tsar Ivan Alexander and wife of Esteban Dušan of Serbia. He was regent by his son Esteban Uroš V and finished his days as a nun.
Hermano de Alejandro V, fue promovido du: Alexander V's brother was promoted during one of his expulsions. His brief government illustrates how factions could replace the king without leaving the same Bagrationi family. His son David II would fight the crown again.
Hermano de Alejandro V, ocupó el trono d: Alexander V's brother, he occupied the throne during another interruption of his government. The competition between the princes of this generation continued later in the rivalry of his son Teimuraz with Solomon I.
Hermano de Amadeo IV, recibió derechos e: Brother of Amadeo IV, received rights in Piedmont and ruled Flanders for his marriage to Juana. He was not his father's successor in Savoy County.
Hermano de Arnaldo Roger I, le sucedió e: The brother of Arnaldo Roger I, his father and his sister, was killed with no children in 1294 and his inheritance was disputed between the Coseran and his niece Sibila.
Hermano de Arnaldo Roger II, recibió el: Brother of Arnaldo Roger II, received the county of Peter IV in 1343 and served the king in the campaigns of the Rosellon (1343) and Majorca (1349).
Hermano de Arnaldo Roger III, fue conde: Brother of Arnaldo Roger III, was Count from 1369 to 1416 and married Blanca de Foix-Castellbó. He served the infant John and in the campaign of Panissars of 1389-1390; after Caspe's commitment he supported Fernando de Antequera and participated in the pacification of the revolt of Jaime de Urgel (1412-1413).
Hermano de Carlos V y fundador de la ram: Brother of Charles V and founder of the Austrian branch of the Habsburg. He brought together Austria, Bohemia and a large part of Hungary and finally succeeded his brother in imperial dignity.
Hermano de David X, asumió la corona des: David X's brother, assumed the crown after his abdication and gave it to his nephew Luarsab. His brief government links two generations of the Bagrationi in a period of growing Persian intervention.
Hermano de Edmundo Tudor y tío de Enriqu: Brother of Edmund Tudor and uncle of Henry VII. He held his place and his nephew was protected while in exile and participated in his expedition of 1485. Henry VII created him Duke of Bedford.
Hermano de Enrique II, lo apartó del gob: Brother of Henry II, he took him away from the government of Cyprus and exercised the administration of the island. His marriage to Isabel of Armenia connected the Lusignan to the Cilicia succession. He was killed, which allowed Henry to return.
Hermano de Enrique III de Inglaterra, fu: Brother of Henry III of England, he was elected King of the Romans by a part of the electors. His candidacy competed with that of Alfonso X of Castile during the imperial interregno.
Hermano de Esteban II y esposo de Jelena: Brother of Stephen II and husband of Jelena Šubić, links the leading families of Bosnia and Croatia. His son Tvrtko inherited the banate as a young man. The participation of their parents in that first stage helps to understand that ownership and exercise of power were not always the same.
Hermano de Gediminas, combinó la guerra: Brother of Gedimas combined the war on orders with the alliance with Riga of 1298. He consolidated Lithuania and its presence in Polotsk; the initial date of his government is approximate.
Hermano de Hetum II, obtuvo la corona tr: Brother of Hetum II, he obtained the crown after the murders of 1307. He tried to hold the kingdom between the Mamluk threat and the search for Western support. The discussions on religious union accompanied his foreign policy.
Hermano de Hugh O’Neill y padre de Owen: Brother of Hugh O'Neill and father of Owen Roe, links the generation of the Nine-year War with that of the Irish Confederation. His family maintained military and matrimonial connections between Ulster and the continent.
Hermano de Luis IV, asumió la dignidad e: Brother of Louis IV, assumed electoral dignity in 1449. His access opened a tutelage and a successor arrangement whose final beneficiary was his nephew Philip.
Hermano de Luis XIII, participó en varia: Brother of Louis XIII, he participated in several conspirations against Richelieu and real politics. His position as a possible heir gave him influence until the birth of the future Louis XIV.
Hermano de Luis XIV, fundó la rama moder: Brother of Louis XIV, founded the modern branch of Orleans. He combined a subordinate position in the court with a prominent military participation, especially in Cassel.
Hermano de Mauricio, elector de Sajonia: Brother of Mauritius, election of Saxony since 1553. He defended Orthodox Lutheranism, reorganized the administration of the electorate and gathered in Dresden a chamber of art and wonders.
Hermano de Miguel Antonio y Juan Ludovic: Brother of Miguel Antonio and Juan Ludovico, he agreed to the marquisate with French support following the successor crisis of 1528. His subsequent approach to the emperor changed that relationship.
Hermano de Nikola VII, fue nombrado ban: Brother of Nikola VII, he was appointed ban in 1665, although his formal installation was delayed until 1668. Together with his brother-in-law Fran Krsto Frankopan, he took part in the aristocratic opposition to the Habsburgs.
Hermano de Otón Enrique, compartió desde: The brother of von Henry, from 1522, shared the government of Pfalz- Neuburg. Between 1535 and 1541 both shared fields of authority within the principality.
Hermano de Pedro I, gobernó durante la m: Brother of Peter I, he ruled during the minority of Peter II. The charges and revenge that followed the king's murder faced the members of the court. His title as Prince of Antioch was nominal, for the principality had disappeared.
Hermano de Salomón I y padre de Salomón: Brother of Solomon I and father of Solomon II. His marriage to Helena, daughter of Heraclio II, linked the last real generation of Imereti to the united monarchy of Kartli@-@ Kakheti.
Hermano de Vajtang VI, obtuvo el trono p: Brother of Vajtang VI, he obtained the throne first with Persian support and then under Ottoman domination. His changes in alliance and confession reflect the struggle for Kartli between the two powers and the factions of the royal family.
Hermano de Vlad III y rival por el trono: Brother of Vlad III and rival for the throne of Wallachia. With Ottoman support he replaced Vlad during the 1462 crisis and embodies the complex policy of accommodation and resistance to Constantinople.
Hermano del cardenal Francesco Pignatell: Brother of Cardinal Francesco Pignatelli. He occupied virreates in Sardinia and Sicily; a virrey administered in the name of the monarchy and was not sovereign of those territories.
Hermano del papa León X, gobernó Florenc: Brother of Pope Lion X, he ruled Florence after the return of the Medici in 1512 and was Duke of Nemours. His tomb, the work of Miguel Ángel, is in the New Sacristy of San Lorenzo.
Hermano y colaborador de Jogaila, fue su: Brother and collaborator of Jogaila, was his lieutenant in Lithuania until the Astrava agreement of 1392. He then received land in Volinia and the Kyiv principality; his delegated office differs from the sovereignty of the grand duke.
Hija de Alain de Albret y Françoise de C: The daughter of Alain de Albret and Françoise de Châtillon, was the sister of John III of Navarre. His marriage to Cesare Borgia was part of the political connections between the French monarchy and the Italian world.
Hija de Alejandro VI y figura central de: The daughter of Alexander VI and central figure of the dynastic alliances of the Borja. After several political marriages he became Duchess of Ferrara and developed an important cultural court.
Hija de Alfonso IX de León y Berenguela: Daughter of Alfonso IX of León and Berengaria of Castile. He married John of Brienne, king of Jerusalem and later Latin emperor of Constantinople.
Hija de Amadeo V de Saboya y esposa de A: Daughter of Amadeus V of Savoy and wife of Andronikos III Paleologist. He was regent by his son John V during the civil war against Juan Cantacuceno (1341-1347).
Hija de Amalarico de Lusignan e Isabel d: The daughter of Amalarico of Lusignan and Elizabeth of Jerusalem, married Lion I of Armenia. She was the mother of Elizabeth, a heiress of the Cilicia crown. This link establishes a direct connection between the first royal houses in Cyprus, Jerusalem and Armenia.
Hija de Arnaldo Roger I, fue condesa de: The daughter of Arnaldo Roger I, he was Countess of Pallars from 1295 to 1330 in front of the claims of the Coserans, with the support of James II. In 1297 he married Hugo de Matapala, who ruled with her.
Hija de Bagrat III de Imericia, su matri: The daughter of Agrat III of Imereti, his marriage with Luarsab I united the two western and eastern branches of the Bagrationi. He was the mother of Simon I and David XI, and his challenges followed different policies with respect to saving power.
Hija de Beka I de Samtsje y esposa de Al: Beka I's daughter and Reg II's wife. The opposition of Andronicus II to this marriage reveals that the family alliances of the Black Sea could contradict Constantinople's plans.
Hija de Bernabò Visconti, se casó con Pe: Bernabò Visconti’s daughter married Peter II to strengthen relations between Milan and Cyprus. Their only daughter died young. After being widowed, she returned to Italy. The Duchess of Orléans was another member of the Visconti family named Valentina.
Hija de Blanca I de Navarra y Juan de Ar: The daughter of Blanche I of Navarre and John of Aragon, and the sister of Charles of Viana and Eleanor. After Charles’s death she stood at the centre of the dispute over Navarrese succession rights against her father.
Hija de Bohemundo V y esposa de Enrique: Daughter of Bohemundo V and wife of Henry I of Cyprus, he exercised the regency of the island by his son Hugo II. His presence in Acre shows how the family alliances of Antioch also influenced the policy of Jerusalem.
Hija de Carlos I de Albret, se casó con: The daughter of Charles I of Albret, married John I of Foix and was the mother of Gaston IV. This marriage connected the Albrets to the Foix-Grailly line before the later link of Catalina de Navarre and Juan III of Albret. His presence reveals a family connection prior to the most well-known regia union.
Hija de Carlos II de Navarra, se casó pr: The daughter of Charles II of Navarre, first married John IV of Brittany and was the mother of several members of the next ducal generation. He later married Henry IV of England.
Hija de Carlos IV de Francia y Juana de: The daughter of Charles IV of France and Joan of Évreux, born a year before his father's death. He died single in 1341.
Hija de Carlos IX y María del Palatinado: Daughter of Charles IX and Mary of the Palatinate. His marriage to Juan Casimiro del Palatinado- Zweibrücken connected the Vasa with a branch of Wittelsbach. His son Carlos X Gustavo succeeded Cristina of Sweden: the change of name did not break the family continuity per female line.
Hija de Carlos de Orleans y María de Clé: The daughter of Charles of Orleans and Mary of Cleves, was the sister of Louis XII of France. His marriage to Juan de Foix turned his sons Germana and Gaston de Nemours into nephews of the French monarch. This family relationship allows us to understand part of the international dimension of their trajectories.
Hija de Carlos de Valois y Catalina de C: Daughter of Charles de Valois and Catherine de Courtenay, he inherited the title of Latin empress of Constantinople, already without territory. Married to Felipe de Tareto, she resided in the angevina court of Naples.
Hija de Diarmait Mac Murchada, su matrim: A daughter of Diarmait Mac Murchada, her marriage to Richard de Clare formed part of the agreement that brought Anglo-Norman aid to Leinster. The rights transmitted through their daughter Isabella connected this Irish inheritance to the Marshal family and the aristocracy of England, Wales and Scotland.
Hija de Enrique I de Inglaterra y viuda: The daughter of Henry I of England and widow of the emperor Henry V. He duchy his throne to Stephen of Blois (1135-1153) and in 1141 his name was "lady of the British," but she was never crowned. The Atlas does not register that title as an effective government.
Hija de Enrique II de Champaña e Isabel: The daughter of Henry II of Champagne and Elizabeth of Jerusalem, married Hugo I of Cyprus. He exercised regency functions and maintained rights and interests linked to both sides of the Mediterranean. His file connects the house of Champagne with Cyprus and Jerusalem, without reducing it to its later Navarre branch.
Hija de Enrique II y Leonor de Aquitania: The daughter of Henry II and Leonor of Aquitaine, married William II of Sicily in 1177. Widow, accompanied his brother Ricardo in the third crusade and in 1196 married Raimundo VI of Tolosa. She died in 1199 and was buried in Fontevraud.
Hija de Enrique IV de Francia y María de: The daughter of Henry IV of France and Mary of Medici, married Victor Amadeo I of Savoy. After his death he defended the government of his children in front of the princes of the ducal family, including Thomas Francis of Carignano.
Hija de Enrique IV de Inglaterra y María: Daughter of Henry IV of England and Mary of Bohun. His marriage to Erik of Pomerania connected the monarchy of Lancaster with Kalmar.
Hija de Enrique de Mecklemburgo e Ingebo: Daughter of Henry of Mecklenburg and Ingeborg of Denmark. His marriage to Wartislaw VII of Pomerania was the link of which Erik and Catalina were born. For Mary, Erik's relationship with Margarita is explained; for Catherine, the next generation took Cristóbal de Bavaria.
Hija de Erik IV de Dinamarca y esposa de: Daughter of Erik IV of Denmark and wife of Magnus VI of Norway. She was the mother of the kings Erik II and Haakon V. After Magnus's death he participated in the government during the Erik minority, in a context of tensions between the crown, the aristocracy and the Church.
Hija de Esteban II Kotromanić, se casó c: Daughter of Stephen II of Bosnia, married Louis I of Hungary. His daughters Mary and Eduviges extended connections with the Hungarian and Polish crowns. Its Bosnian provenance allows it to follow a different family line from that of its cousin Tvrtko, who remained in the front of Bosnia.
Hija de Federico Enrique de Orange y Ama: Daughter of Frederick Henry of Orange and Amalia de Solms. He married John George II of Anhalt-Dessau and exercised regency for his son Leopold I between 1693 and 1698.
Hija de Felipe II e Isabel de Valois, se: Daughter of Philip II and Elizabeth of Valois, married Carlos Manuel I of Savoy. His marriage placed the Duke's descendants within the Habsburg and Valois family network. Among his sons were Victor Amadeo I and Thomas Francis, for whom he continued the branch of Carignano.
Hija de Felipe III de España, esposa de: The daughter of Philip III of Spain, his wife and mother of Louis XIV. Regent of France with Cardinal Mazarino, she passed through the Foundabout without losing his power.
Hija de Felipe de Évreux y Juana II de N: The daughter of Philip of Évreux and Juana II of Navarre, was his wife of Peter IV of Aragon. His marriage linked his new and new house with the Aragonese monarchy.
Daughter of Philip of Evreux and Juana II of Navarre, married Philip VI of France. This marriage brought the Navarre house closer to the first generation of the Valois regia.
Daughter of Philip of Évreux and Juana II of Navarre, married Gaston Fébus. She was the mother of the Count's legitimate son, also called Gaston.

A daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she married Gaston Fébus and was mother to the count’s legitimate son, also named Gaston. Her marriage connected Foix with Navarre, although the breakdown of the marriage and her son’s death prevented her descendants from continuing the male line.
Hija de Felipe el Hermoso y Juana de Cas: Daughter of Philip the Beautiful and Juana of Castile, married Cristian II of Denmark. His marriage connected the Kalmar crisis with the Habsburg network. After Cristian's deposition he accompanied the family to exile in the Netherlands, where he died.
Hija de Gastón IV de Foix y de Leonor de: Daughter of Gaston IV of Foix and Leonor of Navarre, married Francis II of Brittany. She was the mother of Anne of Brittany. Its position allows to travel a direct connection between the pirenaic houses and the Atlantic duchy, without the need to go through the later French marriages of Ana.
Hija de Gastón VII, aportó los derechos: Daughter of Gaston VII, he brought the rights over Bearne to the offspring of his marriage to Roger Bernardo III of Foix. Its role is fundamental to understanding the origin of the heritage union.
Hija de Gian Galeazzo Sforza e Isabel de: The daughter of Gian Galeazzo Sforza and Isabella of Aragon married Sigismund I of Poland in 1518. She influenced the court in Kraków and returned to her Duchy of Bari in 1556, where she died.
Hija de Guido de Dampierre, se casó con: Daughter of Guy of Dampierre, married Floris V of the Netherlands. She was the mother of John I, the last Dutch count of that male line. His marriage linked two neighbouring houses whose heritage would end up gathering long after under the Dukes of Burgundy.
Hija de Guillermo IX y Ana de Alençon, s: Daughter of William IX and Anne of Alençon, her marriage to Federico II Gonzaga was decisive for the transmission of Monferrato to that house. The inheritance required an imperial resolution and was not an automatic effect of the weddings.
Hija de Guillermo Marshal e Isabel de Cl: The daughter of William Marshal and Elizabeth of Clare. Her marriage with Gilbert of Clare linked his family inheritance with his daughter Elizabeth's house and his family's family and his family's Bruce of Scotland.
Hija de Guillermo VIII de Monferrato, se: Daughter of William VIII of Monferrato, married Charles I of Savoy. After the death of the Duke, he took over the regency of his son Carlos Juan Amadeo and defended his authority before the relatives of the house.

A daughter of William VIII of Montferrat, she married Charles I of Savoy. After his death she served as regent for their son Charles John Amadeus and defended her authority against relatives of the house. When the child died in 1496, the duchy passed to Philip II. Blanche belonged to the Palaiologan house of Montferrat, not to the marquesses of Saluzzo.
Hija de Guy de Bretaña y sobrina de Juan: The daughter of Guy of Brittany and niece of John III, he claimed the duchy in front of John of Montfort. Her husband, Charles of Blois, militarily defended his cause.
Hija de Haakon V y Eufemia. Su matrimoni: Daughter of Haakon V and Euphemy. His marriage to Erik Magnusson linked Norway to the Swedish house of Bjälbo. His son Magnus inherited Norway and was elected king of Sweden in 1319. Ingeborg intervened in minority politics, although the councils of both kingdoms then limited their authority.
Hija de Hetum I y esposa de Bohemundo VI: The daughter of Hetum I and his wife from Bohemundo VI. Her marriage strengthened the partnership between Armenia, Antioch and Tripoli and after her husband's death she became involved in the politics of the county during the minority of Bohemundo VII.
Hija de Hugo III de Chipre y esposa de T: Daughter of Hugo III of Cyprus and wife of Theodore III of Armenia, she was the mother of Lion III. His marriage is one of the direct links between the two monarchies, prior to the Lusignan's access to the Cilicia crown.
Hija de Jacobo II y reina de Inglaterra,: Daughter of James II and queen of England, Scotland and Ireland with William III. His access to the throne consolidated the dynastic and political outcome of the Glory Revolution.
Hija de James de Desmond, enlazó a los F: Desmond's daughter, he linked the Fitzgerald to the Butler for his marriage to James de Ormond. After he was sent, he finally married Gerald de Desmond. His family alliances crossed the political rivalry between the two houses.
Hija de Jorge X de Kartli y esposa de Te: Daughter of George X of Kartli and wife of Teimuraz I of Kakheti. The marriage strengthened cooperation between the two branches during their wars against Persia. His children linked this generation to the later kings of Kakheti and Immericia.
Hija de Jovan Branković y esposa de Petr: Daughter of Jovan Branković and wife of Petru Rareș, brought to Moldova the connection with the Serbian despots. He intervened in the government during the minority of his son Esteban. His daughter Ruxandra also became a consort and regent Moldava. Chiajna, daughter of another union of Petru, was his stepdaughter.
Hija de Juan Amor Tarnowski y esposa de: Jan Amor Tarnowski’s daughter and the wife of Konstanty Wasyl Ostrogski. After her brother Jan Krzysztof’s death, her inheritance connected Tarnów with the Ostrogski estates.
Hija de Juan II de Bretaña y Beatriz de: The daughter of John II of Brittany and Beatriz of England, married Philip of Artois. His offspring linked with the Evreux through Margaret of Artois. The Bretaña-Artois-Évreux chain is an important family connection between the Atlantic duchy and the Navarre monarchy.
Hija de Juan Jacobo de Monferrato y Juan: The daughter of John James of Monferrato and Juana of Savoy, married Ludovico I of Saluzzo. His son Ludovico II thus gathered the descent of the Saluzzo, the Italian Paleologists and the Savoy.
Hija de Juan VI Cantacuceno y esposa de: The daughter of John VI Cantatacene and wife of John V Palaiologos, a marriage that sealed peace after the Byzantine civil war of 1341-1347.
Hija de Juan de Borbón-La Marche y Catal: The daughter of John of Bourbono - La Marche and Catalina of Vendôme, married Jano. She was the mother of John II and Anne of Cyprus. This union directly connects the Lusignan with the Bourbon and, by Ana, with the Savoy dynasty.
Hija de Juan de Foix y María de Orleans,: Daughter of Juan de Foix and Maria de Orleans, he was niece of Louis XII of France and second wife of Fernando the Catholic. His position connected the negotiations between France and Aragon with the naval interests of his family.
Hija de Juan de Gante y Catalina de Roet: A daughter of John of Gaunt and Katherine Swynford. Through her marriage to Ralph Neville she was the mother of Cecily Neville and Richard, Earl of Salisbury; her descendants connected the principal Yorkist leaders.
Hija de Juan sin Miedo y hermana de Feli: A daughter of John the Fearless and sister of Philip the Good, she married Adolf of Cleves. She was the mother of Catherine, wife of Arnold of Egmond. That line connected the dukes of Guelders with the Burgundian house that later intervened in its succession.
Hija de Leopoldo VI de Babenberg y de Te: Daughter of Leopold VI of Babenberg and Theodora, Constanza of Austria married Henry III, Margrave of Misnia in 1234. His marriage linked the Babenberg to the Wettin. He was the mother of Alberto and Dietrich; he died in 1243, before the Austrian successor crisis of 1246.
Hija de Levan de Kajetia y esposa de Sim: The daughter of Levan of Kakheti and wife of Simon I of Kartli. His family linked the two Eastern monarchies through their children and grandchildren; these marriages coexisted with political rivalries and with the intervention of Persia and the Ottomans.
Hija de León II y Keran, se casó con Ama: Daughter of Lion II and Karan, married Amalarico of Lusignan. After her husband's death, her family was caught in the struggles of the Armenian court. His descendants inherited the pretense that led the Lusignan to the sackcloth throne.
Hija de Lionel de Amberes y esposa de Ed: The daughter of Lionel of Antwerp and wife of Edmund Mortimer, Count of March. His offspring linked an old branch of Edward III with Anne Mortimer and Richard of York.
Hija de Luis de Orleans y de Valentina V: The daughter of Louis of Orleans and Valentina Visconti, married Richard of Brittany. His son Francis II became a duchy and became father of Anne of Brittany. Through Margarita, that heiress Bretona was connected with families of Orleans and Milan before their own actual marriages.
Hija de Luis de Évreux y Margarita de Ar: Daughter of Louis of Évreux and Margarita of Artois, married Charles IV of France. His marriage connected the branch of Evreux with the main line of the capet kings.
Hija de Manfredo y esposa de Pedro III,: The daughter of Manfredo and wife of Peter III, he retained the dynastic connection between the Hohenstaufen and the new island monarchy. The Vespers made this heritage politically decisive. His sons Jaime and Federico show that Aragon and Sicily could share family without maintaining the same sovereign.
Hija de Manuel I de Portugal y de María: Daughter of Manuel I of Portugal and Maria of Aragon, married his cousin Charles V in Seville in 1526. He ruled Castile during the Emperor's absences and died in Toledo in 1539, after a difficult birth; he was the mother of Philip II.
Hija de María Teresa de Austria y reina: Daughter of Mary Teresa of Austria and queen of France for her marriage to Louis XVI. In prison during the Revolution, she was guillotinated in 1793.
Hija de Miguel VIII y hermana de Andróni: Daughter of Michael VIII and sister of Andronikos II, his marriage to John II brought the courts of Constantinople and Trebisonda closer. He supported the Georgian marriage of his son Alejo II, linking the Paleologists to the Caucasus networks.
Hija de Pedro I de Borbón e Isabel de Va: The daughter of Peter I of Bourbon and Elizabeth of Valois, married Arnaud- Amanieu of Albret. She was the mother of Charles I. Their filiation connects the Albrets with two Capetians and shows how a marriage alliance could add courtesan relations to the territorial heritage of a house.
Hija de Petar Zrinski y Ana Katarina Fra: The daughter of Petar Zrinski and Anne Katarina Frankopan, married Francis I Rákóczi and was the mother of Francis II. He defended Munkács against the imperial forces.
Hija de Petru Rareș y Elena Branković, s: Daughter of Petru Rareș and Elena Branković, married Alexander Lăpușneanu. He intervened in the continuity of his family and, following the withdrawal and death of his husband, exercised the regency of Bogdan IV. Its descent links the Moldovan sovereign with the family of the Serbian despots.
Hija de Petru Rareș y de su primera espo: The daughter of Petru Rareș and her first wife Maria married Mircea Ciobanul. After her husband's death, she directed the policy of her son Petru's government. The dismissal of 1568 led the family to exile. He is still on the news of 1587; there is no known one precise year for his death.
Hija de Reinaldo II, se casó con Guiller: Daughter of Reinaldo II, married William of Jülich and transmitted rights to his children over Guelders. His position explains the access of Jülich's house after the death of his brothers. From his offspring also comes the hereditary bond of Arnold of Egmond.
Hija de Roberto I de Artois, Blanca fue: Daughter of Robert I of Artois, Blanca was Queen consort of Navarre for his marriage to Henry I. When he sent in 1274 he defended his daughter Juana's inheritance and negotiated his link with the future Philip IV of France. His second marriage, with Edmundo de Lancaster, connected the house with the English monarchy.
Hija de Roger IV de Foix, se casó con Ja: The daughter of Roger IV of Foix, married Jaime II of Mallorca. This link connected the Pyrenees house to a monarchy whose heritage was a collection of island and continental spaces. Through its offspring, you can follow the Mediterranean projection of the family of Foix.
Hija de Sancho VI de Navarra, se casó co: Daughter of Sancho VI of Navarre, married Richard I in Limassol (Cyprus) in 1191, in the middle of a crusade. He never lived in England; after he had been sent, he lived in Le Mans, which was part of his dowry, and there he founded the abbey of L'Épau, where it is buried.
Hija de Sancho VI y hermana de Sancho VI: The daughter of Sancho VI and sister of Sancho VII, married Teobaldo III of Champagne. After his death, he held the position of his son Teobaldo during his minority. For her, that son gathered a Navarro hereditary right that became effective when his uncle Sancho VII died.
Hija de Segismundo I de Polonia y Bona S: Daughter of Seisworld I of Poland and Bona Sforza, married John of Sweden, future John III. His son Sigismund brought together the Polish election and the Swedish heritage. The Jagellon- Vasa connection explains that accumulation, but the political and confessional differences ended up separating the crowns.
Hija de Teobaldo I de Navarra y Margarit: Daughter of Teobaldo I of Navarre and Margarita of Bourbon, married Hugo IV of Burgundy. His career extended the connections of the house of Champagne beyond his French and Navarro heritage. It was one of the women that family alliances reached other ducal houses.
Hija de Teobaldo I de Navarra y de Inés: Daughter of Teobaldo I of Navarre and Inés of Beaujeu, married John I of Brittany. She was the mother of John II.
